sounds.name: Jupiter Brass
sounds.ref: Classic early-80s polysynth brass
sounds.blurb: Bright, punchy brass chords with a quick “blat” at the front of every stab.
sounds.how: Two sawtooth oscillators, one tuned a few cents sharp, play every note of the chord. The filter is set to its brighter −12 dB slope and closed part way, and ENV-1 flicks it open and back on each chord, which gives the brassy bite. ENV-2 keeps the volume full while the keys are held.

steps.title: Two sawtooths, slightly apart
steps.why:
Both oscillators play a sawtooth, the brightest wave and the raw material of brass. Detuning one a little gives every note movement.
- VCO-1 and VCO-2 WAVEFORM sawtooth, VCO-2 RANGE at 8’: the two play the same note.
- FINE TUNE +0.8 (+8 cents): VCO-2 a little sharp, so each pair beats slowly. At 0 the chord sounds thinner and stiller.
- SOURCE MIX 5: both oscillators at full level.
- Listen for: a slow swirl in a held chord. Turn FINE TUNE back to 0 to hear it stop.

steps.title: A brighter filter, part closed
steps.why:
The filter’s −12 dB slope leaves more of the upper harmonics in than −24 dB, which suits brass. Closing it part way gives the envelope room to open it.
- SLOPE −12dB/OCT: brighter and buzzier than −24.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4.5 (about 470 Hz): dark between stabs.
- RES 1.5 (15 %): a slight edge at the cutoff.
- KEY FOLLOW 6 (72 %): high notes stay brighter, so the top of a chord does not go dull.
- Listen for: a warm, muted chord, waiting for the envelope.

steps.title: ENV-1 opens the filter
steps.why:
ENV-1 is an ADSR (attack, decay, sustain, release) that runs on every note. Here it pushes the cutoff up and lets it settle: the “blat” of a brass section.
- ENV MOD 5.5 (55 %), selector at ENV-1: how far the envelope opens the filter.
- A 2.5 (19 ms): quick but not instant, like a breath.
- D 5 (320 ms): the length of the bite.
- S 4 (40 %), R 4 (150 ms): held chords stay a little brighter than at rest, and close quickly after you let go.
- Listen for: stabs that bark and then darken. Move ENV MOD between 3 and 7.

steps.title: Shape the loudness
steps.why:
ENV-2 shapes the volume. Brass stabs want full level while held and a clean stop.
- A 1.5 (6 ms): fast, so the chord lands on the beat.
- S 10 (100 %): held chords stay at full level, so D does nothing.
- R 3.5 (100 ms): short, so each stab stops soon after you lift your hands.
- Listen for: the gaps between the stabs. Turn R up to 6 and hear them blur.

context.vcf.env: In this sound: how far each stab opens the filter. Lower for a soft horn section, higher for more bite.
context.env1.decay: In this sound: the length of the bite at the front of each stab.
context.vco2.fine: In this sound: the slight detune that keeps the chords moving.
context.vcf.slope: In this sound: −12 dB keeps the brassy buzz. At −24 it turns rounder and softer.

tweaks.try: Move between 3 and 7 while the chords play
tweaks.hear: From mellow horns to snarling brass.
Rounder and darker, more like a French horn.

sounds.name: Glassy Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of Duran Duran — "Save a Prayer"
sounds.blurb: A held chord turned into a soft, ringing arpeggio climbing two octaves.
sounds.how: The arpeggio plays the held chord one note at a time, upwards over two octaves. Each note is a soft pluck: the filter rests low with a little resonance and ENV-1 opens it briefly, while ENV-2 lets each note ring on into the next. VCO-2 an octave up on a pulse wave adds the glassy top.

steps.title: Start the arpeggio
steps.why:
The arpeggio turns a held chord into a run of single notes.
- MODE UP: the notes play from the bottom up. Press it again to stop.
- RANGE 2: after the first octave the pattern repeats an octave higher.
- RATE 6.5 (7 notes a second): a steady sixteenth-note pulse at about 105 BPM.
- Listen for: a bright saw arpeggio. The next steps soften it into a pluck.

steps.title: A glassy top octave
steps.why:
VCO-2 an octave above VCO-1 on a pulse wave gives each note a bright, glassy edge.
- VCO-1 WAVEFORM triangle: a soft, round base.
- VCO-2 RANGE +12 (4’), WAVEFORM pulse: an octave up, hollow and bright.
- PULSE WIDTH MOD 3 at MANUAL: the pulse a little narrower than square, for a reedier tone.
- SOURCE MIX 4: slightly more VCO-1, so the octave sits behind.
- Listen for: switch VCO-2 back to sawtooth and hear the glass turn to buzz.

steps.title: A soft pluck
steps.why:
ENV-1 opens the low-pass filter for a moment at the start of every note, which makes each one a pluck.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4 (about 340 Hz), RES 3 (30 %): dark at rest, with a slight ring.
- ENV MOD 5 with ENV-1: how far each pluck opens the filter.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 4.5 (220 ms), S 1, R 4.
- KEY FOLLOW 7: the top notes of the run stay bright.
- Listen for: each note now starts bright and settles. Raise RES and the plucks ring more.

steps.title: Let the notes ring
steps.why:
ENV-2 sets how each note fades. A short decay to a low sustain with a longer release lets notes overlap into a shimmer.
- A 0, D 6 (700 ms), S 3 (30 %): each note falls away to a quiet tail.
- R 6 (700 ms): notes keep ringing after the next one starts.
- Listen for: the arpeggio blurring softly into itself. Shorten R to 3 for a dry, clipped run.

context.arp.rate: In this sound: the speed of the run. 6.5 is about 105 BPM in sixteenths.
context.env2.release: In this sound: how much the notes overlap. Longer gives a wash, shorter a dry run.
context.vcf.res: In this sound: the ring on each pluck.

tweaks.hear: A tight figure at 1, a sweeping run across four octaves at 4.
The same notes in a new order every time round.

sounds.name: Shimmering Strings
sounds.ref: Classic polysynth string ensemble
sounds.blurb: Soft string chords that swell in, shimmer while they hold and fade slowly.
sounds.how: Both oscillators play pulse waves whose width the LFO sweeps back and forth, which sounds like many players slightly out of step. The high-pass filter thins out the bottom so the chords sit above a bass part, and slow envelopes make each chord swell and fade.

steps.title: Pulse waves on both oscillators
steps.why:
Pulse waves are softer and hollower than sawtooths, closer to bowed strings.
- VCO-1 WAVEFORM pulse, VCO-2 WAVEFORM pulse: both oscillators on their pulse waves.
- FINE TUNE +1 (+10 cents): VCO-2 slightly sharp, so the chord beats gently.
- Listen for: a reedy, organ-like chord. The next step makes it move.

steps.title: Sweep the widths with the LFO
steps.why:
Pulse-width modulation (PWM) is the shimmer: the LFO sweeps the width of both pulses back and forth.
- PULSE WIDTH MOD switch at LFO, slider 6: how far the width swings.
- LFO RATE 4.5 (about 1 Hz): one sweep a second. Slower drifts; faster warbles.
- Listen for: the chord swirling while it is held. Switch to MANUAL to hear it go still.

steps.title: Thin the bottom, soften the top
steps.why:
The high-pass filter takes away the low end, so the strings do not cloud the bass. The low-pass filter takes the fizz off the top.
- HPF CUT OFF FREQ 4 (about 180 Hz): a lighter, airier chord.
- VCF CUT OFF FREQ 7 (about 2.6 kHz) at −12 dB: warm but still bright.
- KEY FOLLOW 6: high voicings keep their air.
- Listen for: move the HPF slider up and down and hear the weight of the chord come and go.

steps.title: Swell in, fade out
steps.why:
ENV-2 makes each chord swell in like a string section and fade over a second or two.
- A 6.5 (500 ms): a gentle swell.
- S 10: full level while held.
- R 7 (1.3 s): chords hang over into the next.
- Listen for: each new chord rising in while the last one fades.

context.pwm.amount: In this sound: how deep the shimmer is.
context.hpf.cutoff: In this sound: how light the chord is. Down for full strings, up for a thin, airy section.
context.env2.attack: In this sound: how slowly each chord swells in.

tweaks.hear: From a slow sway to a nervous flutter.
The chord thins out into a high, glassy string pad.

sounds.name: Sync Sweep Lead
sounds.ref: Classic oscillator-sync lead
sounds.blurb: A tearing solo lead whose tone sweeps down at the start of every note.
sounds.how: SYNC locks VCO-2 to VCO-1, so VCO-2’s pitch changes its tone rather than its note. ENV-1 sends a pitch sweep to VCO-2 only, so each note starts with VCO-2 high and sweeps down: the tearing sync sound. SOLO and a little portamento make it a mono lead.

steps.title: VCO-2 alone, synced
steps.why:
With SYNC on VCO-2 restarts every time VCO-1 does, so VCO-1 sets the note and VCO-2’s pitch sets the tone.
- SYNC ON.
- SOURCE MIX 10: only VCO-2 is heard; VCO-1 still runs as the clock.
- VCO-2 RANGE +7: a hard, nasal tone. Near 0 it sounds like a plain saw.
- Listen for: turn VCO-2 RANGE while holding a note. The note stays; the tone changes.

steps.title: Sweep VCO-2 with ENV-1
steps.why:
ENV-1 to VCO-2’s pitch, with sync on, is a sweep of tone.
- VCO MOD switch at VCO-2: only VCO-2 moves, so the note stays put.
- ENV MOD 6 (about 2 octaves at the peak): the depth of the sweep.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 6 (700 ms), S 1.5, R 4.
- Listen for: a tearing “neow” at the front of each note.

steps.title: Open filter, one voice
steps.why:
A lead plays one note at a time and slides between them.
- CUT OFF FREQ 7.5, RES 2: open, with a slight edge.
- ASSIGN MODE SOLO: one voice, like a mono synth.
- PORTAMENTO 2.5, switch ON: a short slide between notes.
- Listen for: the slide between notes, with the sweep starting again on each.

context.vcomod.env: In this sound: the depth of the sweep. More gives a longer tear.
context.vco2.range: In this sound: where the sweep settles, so the held tone.
context.env1.decay: In this sound: how long the sweep takes.

tweaks.hear: A quick zap at 4, a slow vowel-like sweep at 7.5.
All eight voices on the one note: much bigger and wider.

sounds.name: Unison Bass
sounds.ref: Classic eight-voice unison bass
sounds.blurb: A heavy, round bass with all eight voices stacked on each note.
sounds.how: UNISON puts all eight voices on one note, each slightly out of tune with the others, so a single bass note is enormous. VCO-1 an octave down adds weight. The 24 dB filter with a short envelope gives each note a round thump.

steps.title: Stack every voice
steps.why:
UNISON is where the weight comes from: all eight voices on the key you play.
- ASSIGN MODE UNISON: one note at a time, eight voices deep.
- Listen for: a thick, slowly churning saw on a low note. Press POLY 1 to compare.

steps.title: A sub octave
steps.why:
VCO-1 an octave below VCO-2 puts a sub under the saw.
- VCO-1 RANGE 16’: an octave down.
- VCO-1 WAVEFORM square: a hollow, woody body under VCO-2’s saw.
- Listen for: the bottom filling out.

steps.title: A round thump
steps.why:
The filter rests dark and ENV-1 opens it at the front of each note.
- CUT OFF FREQ 3.5 (about 240 Hz), RES 2.5.
- ENV MOD 5 from ENV-1: A 0, D 4.5 (220 ms), S 1, R 3.
- Listen for: a “dum” on every note. Sweep ENV-1 D for a tighter or longer thump.

steps.title: Tight loudness
steps.why:
Bass notes should hit at once and stop clean.
- ENV-2 A 0, D 5, S 9, R 2.5 (45 ms).
- Listen for: clear gaps between the eighth notes. Raise R and the line goes soft.

context.assign.mode: In this sound: UNISON stacks all the voices. In POLY the same bass is thin by comparison.
context.vcf.cutoff: In this sound: how much growl comes through between the thumps.
context.env1.decay: In this sound: the length of the thump.

tweaks.hear: Each note gets a rubbery squelch.
Buzzier and brighter: more bite, less weight.

sounds.name: Cross-Mod Bells
sounds.ref: Classic cross-modulation bell
sounds.blurb: Clear, metallic bell tones that ring longer on low notes than high ones.
sounds.how: CROSS MOD lets VCO-2 modulate VCO-1’s pitch at audio rate, which adds the inharmonic overtones of a bell. VCO-2 is tuned to a non-octave interval and kept out of the mix. ENV-2 decays like a struck bell, and KEY FOLLOW makes high notes die away sooner, as on a real bell or piano.

steps.title: VCO-1 alone, as a sine-like tone
steps.why:
The bell starts as a plain tone from VCO-1; VCO-2 will only be heard through the cross modulation.
- VCO-1 WAVEFORM triangle: soft and pure.
- SOURCE MIX 0: only VCO-1 goes to the filter.
- Listen for: a plain flute-like tone.

steps.title: Cross modulation for the clang
steps.why:
CROSS MOD is frequency modulation: VCO-2 wobbles VCO-1’s pitch hundreds of times a second, which turns into new overtones. A non-octave tuning makes them inharmonic, like metal.
- VCO-2 WAVEFORM sine, RANGE +19 (an octave and a fifth up, 4’ + 7).
- CROSS MOD 4.5 (45 %): bright and metallic. More turns into a clang; less, a soft chime.
- Listen for: turn CROSS MOD up slowly and hear the tone turn from flute to bell.

steps.title: Strike and ring
steps.why:
A bell is struck and then rings away, with no sustain.
- ENV-2 A 0, D 8 (2.6 s), S 0, R 7.
- KEY FOLLOW ON (ENV-2): high notes die sooner, low ones ring on.
- CUT OFF FREQ 8.5: the filter stays open.
- Listen for: the low chord ringing much longer than the high notes.

context.vco1.xmod: In this sound: how metallic the bell is.
context.vco2.range: In this sound: the interval of the modulator, which sets which overtones you hear. Try steps away from octaves.
context.env2.kf: In this sound: why high notes are short and low notes ring.

tweaks.try: Step it up or down a semitone at a time
tweaks.hear: Each step gives a different bell, from glassy to gong-like.
The bell turns into a harsh, clanging gong.

sounds.name: Synth-Pop Stab
sounds.ref: In the style of Howard Jones — "What Is Love?"
sounds.blurb: Short, bright chord stabs with a glassy edge, made for off-beat rhythm parts.
sounds.how: A sawtooth on VCO-1 and a pulse on VCO-2 an octave up give a bright, hollow chord. ENV-2 has no sustain, so every chord is a short stab however long the keys are held, and ENV-1 snaps the filter open at the front of each one.

steps.title: Saw and an octave pulse
steps.why:
A sawtooth gives body, and a pulse an octave above gives a glassy top.
- VCO-2 RANGE +12 (4’), WAVEFORM pulse.
- PULSE WIDTH MOD 4 at MANUAL: a little narrower than square, reedier.
- SOURCE MIX 4: VCO-1 a little ahead of VCO-2.
- Listen for: a bright, hollow chord. Turn SOURCE MIX right to hear the octave come forward.

steps.title: A snapping filter
steps.why:
The filter rests fairly dark and ENV-1 snaps it open for a moment at the start of each chord.
- CUT OFF FREQ 5 (about 660 Hz), RES 2.
- ENV MOD 5 from ENV-1: A 0, D 3.5 (100 ms), S 2, R 3.
- Listen for: a bright “tick” at the front of each chord.

steps.title: Make it a stab
steps.why:
With no sustain the chord dies away on its own, so held chords still come out as stabs.
- ENV-2 A 0, D 4.5 (220 ms), S 0, R 3.5 (100 ms).
- VCA LEVEL 10: stabs this short need a little more level.
- Listen for: tight chords that leave room between them. Raise D for a longer, ringing chord.

context.env2.decay: In this sound: the length of each stab.
context.vcf.env: In this sound: how bright the front of each stab is.

tweaks.hear: From a clipped tick to a ringing chord.

sounds.name: Airy Glass Pad
sounds.ref: Classic high-passed pad
sounds.blurb: A thin, shining pad with a slow vibrato that grows in on held notes.
sounds.how: The high-pass filter removes the body of the sound, leaving a light, glassy shimmer. The LFO is set to a slow vibrato, and DELAY TIME makes it fade in only after each chord has been held for a moment, as a player would.

steps.title: Two detuned sawtooths, an octave apart
steps.why:
Two saws an octave apart and slightly detuned give a wide, bright source.
- VCO-2 RANGE +12, FINE TUNE +1.2.
- Listen for: a bright, moving chord.

steps.title: Take the body away
steps.why:
The high-pass filter cuts the low end, leaving only the air on top.
- HPF CUT OFF FREQ 6 (about 430 Hz): the chord loses its weight.
- VCF CUT OFF FREQ 7 at −12 dB: the top is softened a little.
- Listen for: move the HPF slider between 0 and 7 and hear the chord go from full to thin and glassy.

steps.title: A vibrato that grows in
steps.why:
The LFO adds a slow vibrato, and DELAY TIME holds it back for the first part of each chord.
- VCO MOD LFO 0.7 (about a quarter of a semitone), both VCOs.
- LFO RATE 6 (2.8 Hz): a slow, singing wobble.
- DELAY TIME 5 (1.4 s): plain at first, then the vibrato fades in.
- Listen for: each chord starting still and beginning to sway after a second.

steps.title: Slow swell and fade
steps.why:
Slow envelopes keep the pad soft.
- ENV-2 A 6 (350 ms), S 10, R 7.5 (1.9 s).
- Listen for: chords overlapping as they fade.

context.hpf.cutoff: In this sound: how thin and airy the pad is.
context.lfo.delay: In this sound: how long each chord holds still before the vibrato comes in.

tweaks.hear: Vibrato from the start at 0; at 8 only on long chords.
The body comes back and the pad gets warmer.

sounds.name: Inverted Swell
sounds.ref: Classic inverted-envelope pad
sounds.blurb: Chords that start bright, close as they are held and open again as you let go.
sounds.how: ENV-1’s POLARITY switch turns the envelope upside down, so instead of opening the filter it closes it. With slow envelope times the chord starts bright, darkens as ENV-1 rises, and brightens again during the release.

steps.title: A wide, open chord
steps.why:
Two detuned saws and an open filter give a bright chord for the envelope to work on.
- FINE TUNE −1 (−10 cents).
- CUT OFF FREQ 7.5 (about 3.6 kHz), RES 3.
- Listen for: a bright, slightly beating chord.

steps.title: Turn ENV-1 upside down
steps.why:
POLARITY inverted makes ENV-1 close the filter as it rises, instead of opening it.
- POLARITY inverted.
- ENV MOD 6 from ENV-1: how far it closes.
- ENV-1 A 7.5 (1 s), D 7, S 6, R 7.5: slow, so the darkening is a gradual swell.
- Listen for: each chord dimming over a second, then opening again after you let go.

steps.title: Let it ring on
steps.why:
A long release lets you hear the filter opening again after the keys are up.
- ENV-2 A 3, S 10, R 8 (2.6 s).
- Listen for: the bright bloom in the tail of every chord.

context.env1.polarity: In this sound: why the filter closes on each chord instead of opening.
context.env1.attack: In this sound: how slowly each chord darkens.

tweaks.hear: The chords now open as they are held: an ordinary slow sweep.
The chord ducks dark almost at once.

sounds.name: Night Wind
sounds.ref: Classic noise wind effect
sounds.blurb: Gusting wind made from noise, a resonant filter and a slow, wandering LFO.
sounds.how: VCO-2 is switched to NOISE and the mix turned all the way over to it. A resonant filter picks a band out of the noise, and the LFO on RANDOM moves the cutoff about slowly, so the wind rises and falls.

steps.title: Noise instead of a tone
steps.why:
VCO-2’s NOISE setting turns it into a noise source.
- VCO-2 WAVEFORM noise, SOURCE MIX 10: only noise reaches the filter.
- Listen for: a steady hiss on any key.

steps.title: A whistling band
steps.why:
High resonance makes the filter ring at its cutoff, so the noise whistles like wind.
- CUT OFF FREQ 5.5 (about 930 Hz), RES 8, −24 dB.
- Listen for: a hollow, whistling hiss.

steps.title: Gusts from the LFO
steps.why:
The LFO moves the cutoff, and RANDOM makes each gust different.
- LFO WAVE FORM random, RATE 2.5 (0.27 Hz): a new gust every few seconds.
- VCF LFO MOD 6: how far the gusts move the filter.
- Listen for: the whistle sliding up and down at random.

steps.title: Fade in and out
steps.why:
Slow envelopes keep the wind from starting and stopping abruptly.
- ENV-2 A 7.5 (1 s), S 10, R 8.
- VCA LEVEL 10 and VOLUME 9: a narrow band of noise is quiet, so both are turned up.
- Listen for: the wind rising in and dying away.

context.vcf.res: In this sound: how much the wind whistles.
context.lfo.rate: In this sound: how often the gusts change.

tweaks.hear: A softer rush, like surf rather than wind.
Even, regular waves instead of gusts.

sounds.name: Random Bubbles
sounds.ref: Classic sample-and-hold filter
sounds.blurb: A burbling stream of random filter steps on a held note.
sounds.how: The LFO’s RANDOM shape jumps to a new value every cycle. Sent to a resonant filter at a fast rate, those jumps become a stream of bubbles, the classic sample-and-hold sound.

steps.title: A resonant, closed filter
steps.why:
High resonance makes every cutoff jump ring.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4 (about 340 Hz), RES 7.
- Listen for: a dark note with a ringing edge.

steps.title: Random steps on the cutoff
steps.why:
The RANDOM shape picks a new level every cycle; at this rate that is a new bubble about eight times a second.
- LFO WAVE FORM random, RATE 7.5 (7.5 Hz).
- VCF LFO MOD 7: wide jumps.
- Listen for: a stream of bubbling, pitched blips.

steps.title: Track the keyboard
steps.why:
With key follow, the bubbles move with the note you play.
- KEY FOLLOW 8 (96 %).
- Listen for: the bubbles shifting up when the second note plays.

context.lfo.rate: In this sound: how fast the bubbles come.
context.vcf.lfo: In this sound: how wide each jump is.

tweaks.hear: From slow drips to a fizzing stream.
Each step rings like a struck tube.

sounds.name: Plucked Keys
sounds.ref: Classic key-follow pluck
sounds.blurb: A soft, plucked keyboard sound whose high notes are short and low notes ring.
sounds.how: Both envelopes decay to nothing, so every note is a pluck. KEY FOLLOW on both makes the envelopes faster on high notes, as on a harp or a piano, and the filter’s KEY FOLLOW keeps the high notes bright.

steps.title: A soft square
steps.why:
A square on VCO-1 and a pure sine an octave up give a woody tone.
- VCO-1 WAVEFORM square, VCO-2 WAVEFORM sine, RANGE +12: a pure octave on top.
- Listen for: a hollow, organ-like tone.

steps.title: Pluck the filter
steps.why:
ENV-1 opens the filter at each note and lets it fall.
- CUT OFF FREQ 3.5, ENV MOD 6 from ENV-1, A 0, D 5 (320 ms), S 0, R 4.
- KEY FOLLOW 8: high notes keep their brightness.
- Listen for: each note starting bright and mellowing.

steps.title: Notes that die away
steps.why:
No sustain on ENV-2 makes each note a pluck.
- ENV-2 A 0, D 7 (1.3 s), S 0, R 5.
- Listen for: notes fading on their own.

steps.title: Faster at the top
steps.why:
KEY FOLLOW on both envelopes shortens them as you go up.
- ENV-1 KEY FOLLOW ON, ENV-2 KEY FOLLOW ON.
- Listen for: the low notes ringing much longer than the high ones in the rising run.

context.env2.kf: In this sound: why high notes are short and low ones ring.
context.env2.decay: In this sound: how long the notes ring around middle C.

tweaks.hear: Every note now rings for the same time, top or bottom.

sounds.name: Warble Organ
sounds.ref: Classic cross-mod vibrato
sounds.blurb: A reedy organ tone with a fast, rich warble from VCO-2 used as a second LFO.
sounds.how: LOW FREQ turns VCO-2 into a slow oscillator that no longer follows the keys. Through CROSS MOD it wobbles VCO-1’s pitch, a vibrato that runs separately from the main LFO. The mix is turned fully to VCO-1, so VCO-2 is never heard directly.

steps.title: A reedy VCO-1 alone
steps.why:
VCO-1 on a pulse wave is the organ tone; VCO-2 is taken out of the mix.
- VCO-1 WAVEFORM pulse, PULSE WIDTH MOD 3 at MANUAL.
- SOURCE MIX 0.
- Listen for: a plain, reedy chord.

steps.title: VCO-2 as a modulator
steps.why:
LOW FREQ drops VCO-2 to a few cycles a second, and CROSS MOD lets it move VCO-1.
- VCO-2 NORMAL/LOW FREQ at LOW FREQ, WAVEFORM sine, RANGE 22 (about 3.6 Hz).
- CROSS MOD 2.5: a gentle wobble. More turns it into a siren.
- Listen for: a fast, even vibrato on every note.

steps.title: Organ envelopes
steps.why:
An organ is on or off.
- ENV-2 A 0.5, S 10, R 2.5. CUT OFF FREQ 7.
- Listen for: clean starts and stops.

context.vco2.range: In this sound: in LOW FREQ this sets the warble speed.

tweaks.hear: A slow wobble, then a fast flutter.

sounds.name: Singing Lead
sounds.ref: Classic portamento solo lead
sounds.blurb: A smooth, gliding solo lead with vibrato you bring in by hand.
sounds.how: SOLO turns the Jupiter into a mono synth and PORTAMENTO slides between notes. The LFO MODULATION button brings in the performance LFO, a vibrato that rises in over RISE TIME, the way a singer leans into a long note.

steps.title: One voice, sliding
steps.why:
A lead plays one note at a time.
- ASSIGN MODE SOLO.
- PORTAMENTO 3.5 (370 ms), switch ON.
- Listen for: each note sliding into the next.

steps.title: A warm saw tone
steps.why:
Two saws a fifth apart, softened by the filter, give a singing tone.
- VCO-2 RANGE +7, SOURCE MIX 3.
- CUT OFF FREQ 6 (about 1.3 kHz), RES 3, KEY FOLLOW 6.
- Listen for: a full, slightly vocal lead.

steps.title: Vibrato that rises
steps.why:
The performance LFO is a second, sine LFO for playing vibrato.
